conceptZh: 兩隊積木小兵從左右拉扯，一邊拉著「犭」，一邊拉著「師」，拉到彈簧啪地合在一起，積木拼出一隻小獅子在旁邊搖鬃毛。
object: a squad of interlocking toy building bricks in orange, yellow and brown that march, pull a rope and stack themselves into a tiny maned lion
morph: two brick teams tug the left part 犭 and right part 師 of 獅 apart, then a spring pulls them together into one glyph
creativeAngle: 拔河：積木小隊分兩隊拉扯左邊「犭」與右邊「師」，繩子一斷彈簧把兩邊拉合，旁邊積木堆成小獅子甩鬃毛。
promptEn: Create an exactly 8-second animated comedy with a locked frontal camera, bright and playful, no flashing. Setting: a clean solid pale-sky-blue backdrop with a pale cream floor. The only on-screen text is one bold, saturated burnt-orange Traditional Chinese glyph 獅, the left part 犭 beside the right part 師, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins. The lead is a squad of original interlocking toy building bricks (small yellow, red and brown bricks with simple dot faces and tiny stubby legs) that march, stack themselves and topple; no real people. Moment one (0.0-1.8s): two squads of bricks march in from the left and right edges, each squad hauling one end of a thick red rope tied to a floating orange stroke group; the left group is the 犭 and the right group is the 師, and the first spoken 獅 lands as the two squads plant their feet and start to pull. Moment two (1.8-3.4s): the tug-of-war grows wild, the brick squads lean back at an angle, the rope stretches like gum and a small brick at the back is yanked into the air and bounces back down, dizzy; the second spoken 獅 lands as the rope snaps. Moment three (3.4-5.0s): the two halves spring inward on a big coil spring, slam together with a bright click and settle as one perfect 獅, while the brick squads tumble backward into a heap of tiny bricks and then pop up again; at the same moment the word 獅子 is spoken as the loose bricks off to the side stack up into a small lion with a fluffy brick-mane that shakes its head. From 5.0-8.0s the glyph 獅 is completely still, unobstructed and crisp in orange; the brick lion on the floor to the side lifts one stubby paw and sways its mane in a happy wiggle while the squad waves little arms, nobody touching the strokes. Narration (off-screen only, warm Taiwanese Mandarin, slow, distinct, clear tones, no erhua): the voice says exactly 「獅、獅、獅子」, read as ㄕ、ㄕ、ㄕ ㄗ˙, first utterance at about 0.7s, second at about 2.9s, the word at about 4.5s, then stop with no repeats and no extra speech. Only soft brick clicks and a rope twang under the voice, no background music. No subtitles, no vocabulary text, no watermark, no clutter.
